pairs.difference: A: the backboard is a quiet matte white, the frame and rim are satin, and the net cords are soft. Its 0.569 highlight share is the white board area, not gloss. B: the blue sphere and the grey orbit rings share one even airbrushed sheen, with a glowing rim on the ball, so nothing separates the materials. The tiny orange balls have the same finish.
pairs.fix: Make the core a matte painted ball with one small soft highlight, and the rings thin satin metal with a tighter, brighter streak. Remove the glowing edge around the sphere.

pairs.difference: A: the box has a soft leatherette skin with a slightly pebbled edge, the cream lining is matte, and the gold coin is the only shiny thing, which is a real gloss range. B: the tanks carry streaky vertical brushed marks with a noisy grain over them, and the straps have a fine stipple. That is added surface detail, and it looks sharper and busier than the smooth real metal in the lessons.
pairs.fix: Paint the tanks as smooth steel with one clean soft vertical highlight and no brushed streaks. Keep the straps plain matte webbing with no speckle.

pairs.difference: A: dome, wall and trim all share the same smooth satin plaster, and the thin dome seams and sparse block outlines look drawn on instead of cut in. Only the window has any gloss. B: the neon tubes glow against duller painted orange sign boards, and the wooden balcony and brick have their own grain, so the materials differ more.
pairs.fix: Give the dome slightly raised metal panels with a brighter sheen than the matte plaster wall. Cut the block seams into the wall with small soft shadows.

pairs.difference: A: the bottle is frosted translucent plastic, very smooth, with a glossier cap. Its detail is at the bottom of the real range. B: the ball is rubbery with grooved seams, the goal is matte white plastic, and the water is glossy. Both have believable, restrained finishes, and neither shows noise or added micro detail.

A: the petals and stones are puffy lacquered plastic with soft highlights, a toy finish that sits within the soft look of the real cards. B: the book covers are soft and low in gloss, with lightly lined pages and no cloth weave. Gloss is slightly under the real range but the softness matches the real crops. There is no clear surface tell on either card.

A: the panel is crowded with crisp micro parts, including screw heads, rows of LED dots, toggle switches and vent slats, on a faintly speckled, sharpened cream shell. Detail, micro texture, gloss and highlight all sit above the real range. B: this is the real monitor from the lessons, with large soft plastic planes, one small button and a single slot.
pairs.fix: Remove most of the screws, LEDs and vent slats and keep two or three large simple parts. Paint the shell as smooth, slightly soft matte plastic with no speckle or sharpened edges.

pairs.difference: A: green rubbery armour sits against dark lens rims with a fine brushed sheen, and the matte and semi-gloss areas are clearly different, though the rim has some noise. B: the yellow arm has hard sharpened enamel edges, bolts and crisp panel breaks, and the base and floor are also glossy. Detail, micro texture and gloss are all above the real range, and every part has the same crisp finish.
pairs.fix: Soften the edges of the arm and remove the small bolts. Make the yellow shells satin with broad soft highlights, and the dark joints matte rubber.

pairs.difference: A: the crisp glass dome has a hard window highlight, and the seats have fine ribbing. The body has thin scribed panel lines and evenly lacquered teal paint, with sharp chrome trim. Everything is high-gloss, with added fine lines. B: the red scarf is a matte, soft cloth with broad folds and low detail, and only the badge has any shine.
pairs.fix: Remove the thin scribed lines and the seat ribbing. Use softer, broader highlights on the body, make the seats matte, and keep the chrome to a few simple strips.

pairs.difference: A: the pink silicone tray has a frost stipple along its edges and bubbles inside the ice. The specks are fine and fit the subject, even if they are a little noisy. B: the green plastic phone is clean and glossy, with cream keys and a coiled cord. The gloss differences are believable and the measurements are in range, so there is no firm reason to choose.

A: the plane is soft airbrushed white paint with faint panel lines and low detail. Its 0.334 highlight share comes from the large white fuselage. B: the gold box has sharp bright rivets, double-bevelled panel edges, ringed porthole and thin solar-grid lines. All the metal is equally lacquered gold, and detail and micro texture are far above the real range.
pairs.fix: Remove most of the rivets and bevels and leave the box as one soft painted form. Make the gold satin, not lacquered, with a matte dark panel surface and softer grid lines.

pairs.difference: A: the shoes have fine mesh perforation, a matte foam sole and satin laces, so there is a real range of materials, though the card is busy. Its readings sit at the top of the real range. B: the flask has clean glass highlights and crisp, perfectly round bubbles, and the cork is speckled. The bubbles and glass rim are sharper and more decorative than the soft real finish.
pairs.fix: Use fewer, softer bubbles and let the glass highlight fade gently. Make the cork plain and matte, with barely visible speckle.

pairs.difference: A: the tube is misty, airbrushed glass with broad vertical streaks and a blurred glow. The cap and base are one smooth grey sheen, with no surface marks except the glow. B: the post has short carved wood cracks, the rope has a twisted strand pattern, the life ring is glossy and the bands are matte. Each material reads as itself.
pairs.fix: Separate the materials: give the glass one thin sharp highlight, the base brushed satin metal with a slightly duller cap, and the wall a matte finish. Reduce the haze.

pattern: Generated cards give themselves away by adding fine, crisp surface detail that real cards leave out: rivets, screws, LED dots, scribed panel lines, seat ribbing and brushed streaks on metal. The real cards stay soft and low in detail. Generated cards also tend to give every part the same lacquered sheen and sharpened edges, while real cards keep matte plastic, cloth and paint distinct, with gloss saved for one or two parts. The sci-fi subjects show this most clearly (p06, p08, p10). Pairs without that crisp added detail are too close to separate on surface alone.
